name: Familial Hyperaldosteronism

criteria.description: Early-onset hypertension, often resistant to conventional therapy
Elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio indicating primary aldosteronism
Suppression of aldosterone production with dexamethasone administration
Positive family history of early-onset hypertension or hyperaldosteronism
Detection of chimeric CYP11B1/CYP11B2 gene confirming diagnosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early-onset hypertension with elevated aldosterone-renin ratio plus either glucocorticoid suppression test positivity or confirmatory genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is considered the gold standard for definitive diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Hypertension that improves with glucocorticoid therapy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypokalemia due to renal potassium wasting
pathognomonic.notes: Low serum potassium levels despite normal intake

searchTerms: muscle weakness due to low potassium

common.symptomName: Polyuria secondary to hypokalemia-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
searchTerms: excessive urination from kidney issues due to low potassium
increased urine output from kidney resistance

common.notes: Recurrent headaches due to elevated blood pressure
searchTerms: headache caused by high blood pressure
weakness related to salt or mineral problems
abnormal skin feelings related to potassium loss

occasional.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to electrolyte disturbances
searchTerms: cardiac arrhythmias due to low minerals
heart rhythm problems linked to electrolytes

rare.notes: Elevated blood pH due to aldosterone excess

rare.symptomName: Visual disturbances due to hypertensive retinopathy
rare.notes: Blurred vision or visual field defects
searchTerms: vision problems from high blood pressure damage
eye changes due to hypertensive retinopathy
blurred vision from blood vessel damage in eyes
stroke caused by uncontrolled high blood pressure
cerebrovascular event due to high BP

laboratory: Hypokalemia with low urinary potassium excretion
imaging: Adrenal CT or MRI typically normal or showing bilateral adrenal hyperplasia
genetic: Presence of chimeric CYP11B1/CYP11B2 gene fusion detected by PCR or sequencing
other: Suppression of aldosterone secretion with dexamethasone administration

distinguishingFeatures: Caused by renal artery stenosis or volume depletion

redFlags: Severe, treatment-resistant hypertension in young patients
Family history of early-onset hypertension or stroke
